analysis:
The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines ~2336-2348, a Flint constrained-chaining paragraph). The supplied units, head lines 802-1635, are unchanged surrounding context. I found no code, wire-protocol, key-handling or attestation change.

The added text describes CBv2 constrained chaining for FlintNativeProtocolConstraint and FlintAnswerStopConstraint. It says step N+1 is sampled before step N is confirmed, with a redraw from retained logits when the state differs. It also says masks are cached by constraint state (maskCacheKey) and that RecursiveSI/flint-int4 joins the automatic paged list at the legacy serving width on M5 Pro, Max and Ultra.

Security relevance (not findings, because the PR has no code evidence):
- Cached device masks keyed only by constraint state do not hold prompt or tenant data, so they do not touch A-001 or T-041.
- Retained logits and per-row RNG state are transient request-local memory. This is consistent with the T-028 residual-memory posture and does not change it.
- Raising Flint's concurrency on M5 Pro, Max and Ultra through the paged-allowlist entry is a serving-width policy statement. It sits next to the existing note that the concurrency catalogs stay empty until qualification, so the doc's own claim should be reconciled with that.
- The prose claims the token stream is identical to unchained decode. That is an unverified correctness claim, since the implementing code is not in this batch. A divergence would be a correctness or integrity issue (T-007 class), not a confidentiality issue.

The next pass should check whether the corresponding Swift and mlx-swift-lm code changes in other batches preserve the redraw equivalence, the retention and clearing of retained logits, and memory admission for the wider width. Nothing in these two units is a security regression.
